<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:binary-code-packing}
Let $n,d$ be integers with $1\le d\le n$. The binary code packing problem,
whose optimal value is denoted by $A_2(n,d)$, is
\begin{equation*}
\underset{S\subseteq\{0,1\}^n}{\operatorname{maximize}}
\quad |S|
\quad\text{subject to}\quad d_H(x,y)\ge d
\quad\text{for all distinct }x,y\in S.
\end{equation*}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:improved-lower-bounds}
The following lower bounds hold:
\[
 A_2(22,9)\ge84,\qquad A_2(24,9)\ge196,\qquad A_2(25,11)\ge65.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
The complete sets in Section~\ref{sec:verification} contain, respectively, $84$, $196$, and
$65$ distinct words of the indicated lengths. Exhaustive comparison of
all unordered pairs gives minimum distances $9$, $9$, and $11$,
respectively. Each set is therefore a witness
for the corresponding bound.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
